name: South gate
period: late 3rd century AD (c. 270–280): the stone wall as newly built, all gates open
conventions: u along the town wall, v out to the field (so the "n" drawing is the field front); metres; origin the anchor corner

openings.note: outer arch of tile voussoirs: a voussoir tile 17 by 6 in was found here (1890). outer arch carried up as a crenellated parapet on the platform's field side (the parapet: comparison)
inner arch (1890: as the north gate)

platforms.note: "the large platform over the gate itself would enable the defenders to pass from one side to the other" (Fox & St John Hope 1890); at the walk's level, on timber over the passage (the report leaves timber or vault open)

stairs.note: "a rude foundation parallel with the west wall of the gateway, which may have supported a flight of steps having a landing at the top; this would enable the rampart walk to be carried over the gate" (1890); position from Pl. XXXI, the steps themselves conjecture
